reason: E2 directly supports the covariance-based vibrational entropy method for elemental Na and Al above the Debye temperature, but none of the cited evidence provides support for the machine-learning correction step, its extension to multicomponent systems, or the claimed speedup.
premises: Short AIMD ensembles yield a covariance matrix that captures vibrational entropy under a Gaussian approximation.
The covariance-based vibrational entropy is accurate above the Debye temperature for elemental solids.
Machine-learning corrections trained on explicit AIMD data can capture anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling.
The hybrid method can be extended from elemental to binary and high-entropy alloy systems.
The method achieves at least an order-of-magnitude speedup over full AIMD and TOR-TILD.
